correctness.rationale: The frozen proof did not establish its coefficient transfers: its cited Bhowmick–Meher Lemma 2.3 omits the complex-sector condition, and real-axis asymptotics with monotone coefficients alone do not imply the displayed coefficient conclusion (Bringmann–Jennings-Shaffer–Mahlburg, Theorem 1.1, Remark 1 and §3.2). This was a proof gap, not a counterexample to the claim. The complete replacement /workspace/repairs/1/RESULT.md applies the eta transformation to each factor for Re z>0. In fixed sectors the transformed products are exponentially close to 1, the linear exponent cancels, and the result is ell^(-1/2) exp(mu/z) times 1+o(1), hence bounded in modulus by a constant times exp(mu/|z|). The exact nonoverlined-removal bijection gives the shifted-count ratio even at empty or impossible weights. Telescoping the s-th powers of consecutive admissible integers gives the weighted generating series; the Gaussian Stieltjes limit for its factor H_s uses bounded gaps, the quadratic weight sum, and an integrable dominating Gaussian in the tails. This works also at 0<s<1 since d(y^s) has finite mass near zero. Positivity yields |H_s(e^-z)|<=H_s(e^-Re z)=O(|z|^(-s/2)) in those sectors, so both genuine Ingham transfers apply. Adding a nonoverlined 1 is injective and nondecreasing in mex, and both series converge in the open unit disk. Dividing the coefficient equivalents yields Gamma(1+s/2)a^(-s/2); the stated mean, positive variance, and aggregate coefficient follow. The Rayleigh comparison follows by expanding the shifted square-root exponent and is no longer an originality claim. The frozen script was inspected, not run; its enumeration of s=1,2 at finite weights cannot replace the asymptotic proof. Fixed ell and s only; no local result or convergence rate.

originality.rationale: Pass applies only to the repaired fixed-weight positive-real-moment theorem. The frozen headline gave distinct credit to an exactly covered Rayleigh marginal; Resultary 96650212350f proves it at the same fixed ell and with the same treatment of overlines and already gives the exact survivor on the diagonal. This is verified equivalent coverage, not an inference of temporal priority from the same date. The replacement explicitly credits both statements and keeps only the fixed-weight moment strengthening and its aggregate consequence at ell>=4. The nearest joint result only states weak convergence and gives selected moment estimates in its distinct Boltzmann ensemble; it gives tools from which the new conclusion can be derived with further fixed-weight control, not a theorem on all fixed-weight moments or a specialization with that conclusion.
residual_risks: Chronological priority between same-day records is unresolved; both the known joint marginal and exact fixed-weight tail are excluded from the repaired novelty claim.

A broader, unindexed theorem on moments for conditioned marked multiplicities could subsume the remaining result. The standard alternate derivation from coefficient estimates also limits the methodological distinction.

value.rationale: The fixed-width regular-overpartition model has slowly growing excludants, and a marginal weak law alone provides no mean or variance control. The all-positive-real asymptotics settle the aggregate first-moment question across the missing moduli and give tail-sensitive moment constants, including variance, for a previously studied statistic. The value of the repair is that fixed-weight unbounded-observable conclusion, not a second naming of the already covered Rayleigh marginal and not a new Tauberian technique.
